doc.title: John LaPorta interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: Stan Kenton and the summer jazz camps
summary: LaPorta describes the Kenton summer camps conceived by Ken Morris, with hundreds of high school students per camp.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well you have been in both worlds, the performing jazz world and the jazz education. In fact you and Stan Kenton and a couple of other people really were on the ground floor of jazz education.
Are you speaking about the Summer Jazz Camps?

Yeah. Stan Kenton was the head of it. It was really thought of and run by Ken Morris. But Stan Kenton was the head of the camp then. They were wonderful camps. They were really a beginning. Ken Morris was a ballroom operator. And he talked to Buddy Morrow and asked him, he said, “You know I see this disappearing and I’m making money off rock groups now, and I’d like to see what I could do with it.” And he says, “Why don’t you start a summer camp for high school students?” And he thought that was a good idea and got started with it, and we had upwards of 250 students per camp, they usually ran about a week apiece, and had as many as four, five, six summer camps in different locations at colleges or university campuses.
